evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the stakeholder need (to create a game and provide identifying data) without prescribing concrete UI widgets or low-level technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Describes an intended way to invite people (URL) but frames a user-level need rather than low-level UI widgets or implementation internals.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete UI widget (a single multi-line text field) rather than stating the stakeholder need to provide the item to be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States the informational need (see all items) without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes the stakeholder action/need without mandating specific UI widgets or implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to add items; does not prescribe UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to edit items; not prescribing UI widgets or implementation choices.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: A user-level need (remove an item) without technical or UI-level prescription.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: States the desired behavior/need (showing estimates immediately) but does not prescribe concrete UI widgets or low-level implementation.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Defines a stakeholder decision rule (accept average) rather than prescribing UI widgets or technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a specific automatic behavior/implementation rule (auto-fill when condition met) rather than focusing on the stakeholder need to speed acceptance generally.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the stakeholder need to record the agreed estimate without prescribing UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: States a user need (re-estimate earlier story) and does not prescribe low-level solutions.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a useful import capability; although it names a source (spreadsheet), this describes a stakeholder need to bulk-add stories rather than prescribing internal implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Describes a practical way for users to get started quickly; this is a user-facing method rather than a low-level technical implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the informational need (browse history) without prescribing widgets or implementation mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States the need to see a transcript; does not mandate file formats or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a concrete storage/export format (HTML file) instead of stating the higher-level need to save transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete storage/export format (CSV) rather than the stakeholder need to further process or export transcripts in general.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user need (removal of stored data) without prescribing implementation details or storage formats.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Specifies required account data fields (stakeholder need to create an account); this is a user-level data requirement, not a low-level implementation or UI widget mandate.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Describes an expected authentication method from a user perspective; while it names credentials, it does not mandate internal authentication mechanisms or specific UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: States a user need (update account) without prescribing UI widgets or technical solutions.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the privacy/retention need to remove account data; not prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Describes a user-facing requirement (local time display) without mandating internal implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a recovery channel (email) but frames a user-level need to regain access rather than low-level implementation internals.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete algorithmic/scale choices (specific estimation sequences) instead of stating the higher-level need for configurable estimation scales.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: States a user-level constraint (team size limit) without mandating a specific technical approach.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Describes how a user participates (providing a display name) rather than prescribing UI widgets or internal implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an informational need; does not prescribe specific UI widgets or technology.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the user's need for context (list of items) without requiring implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: States the stakeholder need to track who has given estimates; does not mandate low-level UI widgets or technologies.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Describes the desired synchronized reveal behavior but does not prescribe UI widgets or internal implementation specifics.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: States the user need to revise estimates before reveal; this is a functional constraint rather than a low-level implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an informational need (view history) without prescribing how to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to know attribution of estimates; does not mandate specific UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Defines a visible timing feature and its purpose; although concrete about duration, it is a user-facing need rather than low-level implementation prescription.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies desired timer behavior for usability; this is a functional requirement, not prescribing specific UI widgets or internal algorithms.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: States the informational/navigation need without mandating implementation details or widgets.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a consistent ordering requirement (usability need) rather than prescribing an internal rendering mechanism.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Defines the user's ability to change estimates (functional need) without low-level technical prescriptions.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific UI element and its placement (small thumbnail near cards) rather than stating the higher-level need to make the experience more personal.

evaluations.evidence: written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Specifies explicit technical/standards-level implementation constraints (XHTML/CSS compliance) rather than a stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Describes a documentation need to improve shared understanding, without prescribing UI widgets or low-level technical details.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a low-level technical implementation action (creating database indexes) rather than expressing the underlying performance need.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete platform/browser targets (technical constraints) instead of focusing on the stakeholder need for broad browser compatibility at a higher level.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes compliance with specific technical standards (W3C accessibility guidelines) rather than stating the higher-level accessibility needs of stakeholders.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Defines a user-perceived performance need without prescribing implementation details or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: States the user need to use any language; though technical in nature, this is a platform-level capability requirement rather than prescribing an implementation detail.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Describes a usability/Transparency requirement for URLs without mandating how they must be implemented internally.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a user-facing need (trust through good error pages) without prescribing specific UI widgets or technical internals.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: States a privacy requirement (non-identifiable storage) which is a stakeholder need; while it implies technical measures, it does not prescribe a specific storage format or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Specifies an informational/analytics need without prescribing specific technical mechanisms or formats.
